title: Cursor Ultra Plan Pricing: Cost and Limits (2026)
summary: Cursor Ultra plan pricing is $200 monthly, with specified monthly request limits, API access level, and support tier.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


Each answer comes back to one habit: find the unit your plan meters, then watch it before you look at the price.


### Whether Ultra is worth it and how to switch


Is Cursor Ultra worth $200 a month, **putting its annual cost at $2400** ? Only if you run agents most working days and a cheaper tier's allowance keeps running out.


Otherwise you're paying for headroom you won't use. Check how much of your current tier's meter you consume in a normal month. If you rarely finish near the top, Ultra buys nothing.


Can I switch between Cursor plans mid-month? Generally yes, and that makes upgrading a cheap experiment. Try the higher tier for one heavy stretch, then drop back.


Confirm in your billing settings how the change is prorated and when it takes effect, because that decides whether a short trial costs a full month.


### Annual and student discounts


Does Cursor offer a discount for annual billing or students? Cursor has offered both at various times, but terms change, so read the current pricing page rather than trusting a roundup.


Either one lowers the sticker price without changing the allowance. A discounted tier you outgrow in week two still costs you more than the right tier at full price.


### Hitting the usage limit


What happens when I hit my Cursor usage limit? Work slows, moves to a lesser allowance, or stops until the meter resets, depending on your plan and settings. You have more to lose when you find out mid-task than when you check ahead.


Copy the habit of a queue dashboard like Bull-Board. It splits work into active, waiting and failed, and the totals at the top show whether jobs arrive faster than they clear.


A large waiting count beside a small active one means a backlog is forming, so you act before failures pile up.


Read your usage meter the same way, and decide before the limit arrives whether you'll wait, downgrade the model, or pay for more.


### The free plan


Is there a free Cursor plan that is still useful? Yes, for trying the editor and for light, occasional work.


It's a poor fit for daily agent sessions, because those exhaust a small allowance quickly. Use it to learn how much you actually consume.
